messages:
maya: heads up — noticed a bunch of 413s and quota rejects during the canary this morning, looks tied to route-table refreshes :thinking_face:
kevin: saw same in traces, spikes exactly when routing epoch bumped. requests that started before flip sometimes get routed to new pool and get charged against new epoch quota
olga: does the ingress preflight use the canonical route id or do we recompute after we fetch KV? if recompute, that could explain double-charge behavior
sam: telemetry detail — metrics pipeline currently keys usage by (route_id, epoch). when the epoch increments mid-request our emit path writes to the new epoch key. old epoch counter isn't incremented, so console shows big variance and sometimes the new epoch quota is already full
rachel: UX-wise console looks like "sudden surge" in the new epoch which is confusing. customers see quota consumed before their next window even if they sent requests earlier
kevin: quick reproduction: send long streaming embed request that holds connection ~4s while route table TTL (we use 2s) flips. half the token emissions attributed to old route, half to new. clients that retry get 429/413 depending on which epoch they hit
maya: dropping a short repro snippet — run this from a machine hitting canary

```
# curl-ish pseudo repro
for i in 1..50; do
  curl -N -H "X-Embed-Dim: 1536" -H "X-Client-Session: test-epoch" \
    -d '{"input": "long text..."}' https://api.redwood/c/embeds/stream
  sleep 0.05
done
```

kevin: server log sample when it flips:

```
[1.234] route_select: route_id=R12 epoch=41
[1.235] emit_tokens: route_id=R12 epoch=41 tokens=12
[1.239] route_refresh: new_epoch=42 route_id=R34
[1.240] emit_tokens: route_id=R34 epoch=42 tokens=8
```

olga: two related problems: attribution (metrics/console) and enforcement (quota checks). enforcement is naive: we check against current epoch counters at emission time, so mid-flight flips can cause immediate enforcement against new epoch quota even though request started earlier
sam: proposal A: make route selection sticky for request lifetime — pick route_id+epoch at ingress and attach header `X-Embed-Route` so downstream enforcement and metrics use that canonical id
rachel: proposal B (less invasive): have enforcement read both epoch counters and allow a grace window when a request's initial selection maps to an older epoch. then backfill metrics to the origin epoch when we see the incoming header
kevin: metric pipeline change: add `initial_route_id` tag if present, and don't create a new epoch key for short-lived flips (<500ms). but this introduces complexity in aggregation and retention costs
maya: from infra POV sticky selection sounds simplest and most deterministic. header propagation required across internal proxies though. how invasive is that for dedicated/private paths?
kevin: small change: set `X-Embed-Route` on edge and downstream proxies honor it. dedicated/private already pass through headers for KMS/audit, should be fine. need a canary to validate no header stripping
deploy-bot: canary rolling out: canary/embeds-route-sticky v2 -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% (triggered by @kevin) :rocket:
metrics-bot: alert suppressed: spike correlated with canary start at 5950012300, see dashboard panel "embed_route_epoch_shift"
olga: action items —
- implement sticky route header on edge (kevin)
- downstream enforcement to prefer `X-Embed-Route` if present (olga)
- metrics pipeline add `initial_route_id` tag (sam)
- console note/annotation for canary windows (rachel)

maya: +1. will schedule a 30m ops window to roll sticky header canary and watch quotas/dashboards. will paste links to the dashboard after I pin them
kevin: one more thought — also add `X-Embed-Route-Selection-Ts` to help debug ordering when people open tickets
maya: great, let's aim for canary tonight. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
